investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Unschedulable: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector." No pod reached a running state, so no VM was allocated, and the eval runner collected zero evidence — all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are missing.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. Of the 6 total nodes, 4 do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector at all, and the remaining 2 have insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on those nodes. As a result, every remote-agent pod is stuck unscheduled, no VM is provisioned, and the eval runner never receives a vmIdPresent or remoteState value to satisfy the expected-output contract.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready'], neither of which can be satisfied without a scheduled pod.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two affinity-eligible nodes: existing remote-agent pods or other workloads have consumed all available VM slots on those nodes, leaving no capacity for new probe pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 non-matching nodes may have had labels removed or the pod spec's nodeSelector/affinity may have been tightened, reducing the eligible node pool to only 2 nodes and concentrating pressure on them.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: the total kata.peerpods.io/vm quota across the cluster may be too small to absorb concurrent probe runs plus production workloads, causing transient exhaustion during peak scheduling windows.

Lower probability — a stuck or leaked remote-agent pod from a previous probe run that was not cleaned up (withCleanup in the runner) may be holding a VM slot on one of the two eligible nodes, preventing new scheduling.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If a re-run of the eval immediately succeeds and returns vmIdPresent=true with a valid remoteState, the exhaustion was transient and has self-resolved, disproving a persistent capacity problem.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-14T00:12–00:17Z with identical Kubernetes scheduler messages indicating that the 6-node cluster has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity (only 2 nodes carry this resource, both at limit) and 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no agent pod could be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so zero required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) were collected and the expected-output contract was fully violated.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it, and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Every remote-agent pod submitted during the eval window was left Unschedulable for 133–148 seconds before the eval timed out. Because no pod reached a running state, the eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1905: createAgent) could not create an agent, and consequently none of the four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) were produced. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents VM pool, not a code defect in the eval runner or contract definitions. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to the observability eval at this time.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Unschedulable: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector." No pod reached a running state, so no VM was allocated, and the eval runner collected zero evidence — all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are missing.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. Of the 6 total nodes, 4 do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector at all, and the remaining 2 have insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on those nodes. As a result, every remote-agent pod is stuck unscheduled, no VM is provisioned, and the eval runner never receives a vmIdPresent or remoteState value to satisfy the expected-output contract.
proof: failed-check.message: 'pod stuck unscheduled for 133s (Unschedulable): 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical Unschedulable message, pod stuck for 148s, confirming the scheduling failure is not isolated to a single probe run.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable message, pod stuck for 145s, confirming all three remote-agent checks hit the same infrastructure constraint.
failed-check.evidence: empty object — the runner collected no evidence at all, consistent with the pod never reaching a schedulable state.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, confirming the probe never progressed past pod scheduling.
source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) which must schedule a pod before any evidence can be written.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready'], neither of which can be satisfied without a scheduled pod.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two affinity-eligible nodes: existing remote-agent pods or other workloads have consumed all available VM slots on those nodes, leaving no capacity for new probe pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 non-matching nodes may have had labels removed or the pod spec's nodeSelector/affinity may have been tightened, reducing the eligible node pool to only 2 nodes and concentrating pressure on them.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: the total kata.peerpods.io/vm quota across the cluster may be too small to absorb concurrent probe runs plus production workloads, causing transient exhaustion during peak scheduling windows.

Lower probability — a stuck or leaked remote-agent pod from a previous probe run that was not cleaned up (withCleanup in the runner) may be holding a VM slot on one of the two eligible nodes, preventing new scheduling.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If a re-run of the eval immediately succeeds and returns vmIdPresent=true with a valid remoteState, the exhaustion was transient and has self-resolved, disproving a persistent capacity problem.

If kubectl describe on the two affinity-eligible nodes shows kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity is available and no pods are consuming it, the root cause is not resource exhaustion but rather a scheduler plugin bug or misconfiguration.

If the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource does not appear in node capacity at all, the failure may be a missing device plugin registration rather than exhaustion.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used capacity on all eligible nodes before attempting remote-agent creation, surfacing resource exhaustion as a distinct 'warn' or 'fail' signal rather than a scheduling timeout.

Add a stuck-pod detection eval that lists Pending remote-agent pods older than a configurable threshold (e.g., 60s) and fails if any are found, catching leaked probe pods before they exhaust VM capacity.
Add a historical trend eval for remote-agent-create latency to detect gradual capacity degradation before full exhaustion occurs.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-14T00:12–00:17Z with identical Kubernetes scheduler messages indicating that the 6-node cluster has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity (only 2 nodes carry this resource, both at limit) and 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no agent pod could be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so zero required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) were collected and the expected-output contract was fully violated.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it, and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Every remote-agent pod submitted during the eval window was left Unschedulable for 133–148 seconds before the eval timed out. Because no pod reached a running state, the eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1905: createAgent) could not create an agent, and consequently none of the four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) were produced. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents VM pool, not a code defect in the eval runner or contract definitions. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to the observability eval at this time.
